correctness.rationale: For each color, presence in every layer is equivalent to a monochromatic directed cycle, giving exact one-color and two-color intersection counts and vanishing higher intersections. This proves the polynomial for every integer palette. The sign argument excludes all positive zeros other than one and proves simplicity at zero and one. For odd cycle length, exactly two positive auxiliary-variable zeros are guaranteed by two sign changes and capped by exactly two Descartes variations; for even length the negative-input expression is positive. The complete proof is present in RESULT.md, independently corroborated by finite explicit graph tests in verify.py.

value.rationale: The natural first nontrivial independent-twin blowup of a directed cycle gives an infinite family of strongly connected oriented digraphs with an exact two-versus-four real-root transition depending only on parity. This is structurally informative for current research on dichromatic root geometry, provides precise benchmark polynomials, and is not merely a small finite computation or a scalar coloring number. The full root classification requires an independent sign-and-Descartes proof beyond the initial elementary inclusion-exclusion.
